comparator.academicYear: Current official prospective year pages checked 2026-09-25; no entrant-cohort guarantee
comparator.route: Ordinary three-year bachelor with two chosen thematic modules
comparator.sourceNotes: The official year pages supply 60+60+60=180 EC. The first year comprises 11 compulsory religious-studies courses totaling 60 EC, excluding zero-credit Instruction and RADAr. The second year has 45 EC compulsory religion-specific theory, research and applied coursework plus a 15-EC module/free-minor choice. This coherent route selects the first official listed Religie en Zorg module (three 5-EC courses). The third year has 5 EC compulsory humanities practice, a 10-EC required thesis, one selected 15-EC Worldviews, Climate and Nature module (first listed) and 30 EC of genuine free minor space. The university says students complete at least two thematic modules in the bachelor and have 30 EC of free minor space in total; this route has one module in each of years two and three, leaving two 15-EC free minor slots in year three. The year-three page displays multiple possible modules and two free-minor slots simultaneously as options; counting all as mandatory would exceed 60 EC. An alternative valid route may distribute module and free-minor credits differently. The 30-EC teaching minor is an optional instance of the free space, not a required teacher qualification.

alternatives.label: Worldviews, public life & cultural heritage
alternatives.concept: Study belief and meaning through philosophy, myth, literature, archaeology and visual heritage, then examine rights, migration, identity, public institutions and political conflict through law, sociology, psychology and politics. This is a related-fields response: it does not provide sustained study of religious traditions, theology, sacred texts or religious-studies methods.
alternatives.labelReason: The programme devotes substantial space to philosophical and cultural interpretation, heritage, and political-social analysis. Its title states those related fields and does not imply a Religious Studies degree.
progression: Introductory law, philosophy, sociology, politics and archaeology precede advanced constitutional, social-theory, conflict, heritage and interpretive work. Law, Society & Justice precedes Comparative Constitutional Law. All courses use exact planned terms; seven are at 300 level.

alternatives.label: Belief, media & public discourse
alternatives.concept: Examine how media, rhetoric, film, documentary, popular culture and misinformation shape belief, meaning, identity and public debate, supported by philosophy, sociology, social psychology and politics. This direction responds to religion-and-media and conspiracy interests without treating general media study as specialist study of religion.
alternatives.labelReason: Thirteen media, communication, rhetoric, literature and misinformation courses make mediated belief and public discourse the programme centre; sociology, psychology, philosophy and politics provide the social analysis.
progression: Film, rhetoric, philosophy, sociology, social psychology and qualitative-method foundations precede advanced media, communication, social theory, extremism, emotion and conflict work. Every course is offered in its assigned term; nine are at 300 level.
alternatives.distinctness: The first programme combines philosophy, law, politics and material and visual heritage. This direction centres media forms, rhetoric, misinformation and public discourse. The programmes share ten courses and each contains fourteen courses, or 105 EC, absent from the other.

selection.assessment: The closest programme combines philosophical and cultural study of belief with law, politics, sociology and heritage. A second, substantively different media-and-public-discourse route is feasible and replaces fourteen courses. The next direction, worldviews and climate, cannot sustain a religion-linked 24-course programme because UCR environmental courses lack the required worldview and religious-studies framing. The healthcare direction fails for the same religion-specific gap. Production stops at two.

notes.text: Radboud Religion, Politics and Society provides sustained study of religious traditions, sacred texts, theology, sociology and anthropology of religion, religion-specific empirical research, thematic modules and a final work. UCR can study belief and meaning through philosophy and cultural heritage, and it can analyse identity, migration, rights, media and conflict through related fields. These programmes do not reproduce a Religious Studies curriculum.

The external programme contains a fixed Religious Studies major, two selected 15-EC thematic modules, 30 EC of free minor space and a 10-EC final work. UCR assembles related perspectives across individually selected courses and has no scheduled religion-specific thesis; optional independent research is shown separately.
